items.summary: The Apache-2.0 Rust CLI gives any coding agent computer use on macOS, Windows and Linux by reading the operating system's accessibility tree instead of screenshots; a 52-step Apple Maps task dropped from about 198,000 tokens to 31,000. It is the desktop extension of Vercel's agent-browser, and the same bet as [[2026-10-28#3|HiSTEVE playing Minecraft through the game's own interface]]: use the human-facing controls rather than a bespoke API.
items.title: Vercel Labs open-sources agent-desktop, driving desktop apps through accessibility trees

items.summary: Each hair card is a single token and a set diffusion transformer denoises all of them together, producing both the cards and the spring-bone chains that animate them from a single image. On CHARM's own test set it cuts Chamfer distance by 44% and more than halves card-orientation error while running 33 times faster, and beats CHARM, image-to-3D pipelines and strand-based methods from single images.
items.title: HairDeck generates animation-ready hair cards from one image, 33x faster than CHARM

items.summary: On an expert-annotated benchmark a general-purpose editor returns no usable result in more than 40% of cases, and no single judge is reliable across edit types. EditAgent routes each step to general or specialised editors, attaches a verification record to every candidate — which lets off-the-shelf VLM judges beat finetuned reward models — and judges parallel candidates in one listwise call, which experts preferred in 78.5% of decided comparisons at no more than half the judge calls.
items.title: EditAgent: general image editors fail outright on over 40% of expert-annotated edits

items.summary: The rectified-flow transformer reads the input, allocates capacity and routes tokens by the role each plays, rather than tokenizing uniformly. On ImageNet-512 it improves FID by 2.84 over the matched control with 3.9% fewer FLOPs and comes within 0.69 FID of JiT-B/16 at 38.2% lower cost, and on text-to-image it beats JiT-B/8 on DPG-Bench by 1.06 at 40.6% lower forward cost.
items.title: SpecSlot couples tokenization to token roles in pixel-space generative transformers

items.summary: The benchmark puts 86 equity-research assignments against a database of 3.43 million document versions, so an agent sees only what was published at the time. GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 lead overall at 68.1 and 66.9 out of 100, but Astra reaches only 52.5 on the Forecast & Model component — the part that cannot be retrieved.
items.title: Investor's Last Exam: frontier agents score 52.5 on forecasting when denied hindsight

items.summary: Qwen's benchmark distils 273 multimodal collaborative-coding tasks from 37,463 deduplicated queries over 26,314 real user sessions; the strongest of ten model endpoints passes 69.9% of criteria per task on average yet fully satisfies just 26.4% of tasks, and every endpoint does worse on repository edits spanning three or four change types than on one or two. It is the same per-criterion versus per-deliverable gap [[2026-10-30#8|Replit's ViBench 2.0 found at the whole-product level]].
items.title: Co-Design Bench: best coding agent satisfies 69.9% of criteria but only 26.4% of tasks

related.label: GitHub Octoverse: 40% of PRs start with an agent

items.summary: The MIT-licensed prototype monitors a GitHub repository and optionally Feishu group chats, spawns parallel Worker sessions behind a Router and answers with pull requests rather than waiting to be prompted; it drew roughly 4,000 GitHub stars within a day. It is DeepSeek's entry into the agent-initiated development that [[2026-10-30#4|GitHub measured at more than 40% of pull requests]].
items.title: DeepSeek open-sources Super-Agent, a coding agent that watches repositories and team chat

2026-11-02.lead: OpenAI shipped GPT-Rosalind-6, a biology and drug-discovery model built on GPT-6 Astra's weights that roughly doubles its predecessor's scores on medicinal-chemistry and genomics evaluations, and released it only to vetted laboratories.
2026-11-02.window: 1 Nov 07:00 → 2 Nov 07:00 JST (+ late catches from 26–30 Oct)

items.summary: Eleven domains (chip design, cybersecurity, biology, finance, legal, quant trading, recursive self-improvement, hardware design, materials science, alignment, software engineering) built with 14 specialised RL-environment partners, graded pass@1 over three attempts with an 8-hour default limit and models run in their native harness. Claude Opus 5.5 leads overall at 12% and wins quant trading, hardware and chip design; GPT-6 Astra wins recursive self-improvement and materials science; Gemini 4 Carbon is the only other model in the same range and the strongest on biology, which qualifies its lead on [[2026-10-29#0|Artificial Analysis]]. SemiAnalysis says the safety classifiers of Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra depress their own overall scores.
items.title: SemiAnalysis launches GDPx: best model scores 12%, finance and legal score zero

items.summary: MIT CSAIL report GPT-6 Astra reading Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights, locating a repetition-inducing direction in layers 15 and 19, and subtracting it from 131,072 of 0.8B weights (0.016%) with no gradient training: MATH-500 goes from 7.9% to 48.1%, GSM8K from 13.8% to 67.1%, IFEval from 21.0% to 62.3%, and the token-limit rate falls from 93.0% to 33.1%. Astra also named the game four toy policy networks were trained on from weights alone and, on 9x9 Go, beat an equal-sized PPO network trained on 20 million games. The authors call the results very early; a Gemma 3 270M control showed no gain, and a same-day rebuttal argues the Qwen edit is what a competent human researcher would have done.
items.title: GPT-6 Astra edits 0.016% of a model's weights and lifts its MATH-500 score 6x

items.summary: A theoretical account of 'conditional interaction', in which a cheap predictor screens which interactions get executed by the expensive model. Under ideal screening and equal execution costs, execution compute falls by a factor approaching 1/ρ_u, where ρ_u is the density of utility-relevant interactions, and selection regret is bounded by predictor error and the utility margin. No benchmark results.
items.title: Tsinghua paper derives how much compute a predict-gate-execute loop saves

items.summary: Built on the post-trained Gemma 4 26B-A4B checkpoint via online distillation, it reports 98.90 on Big Bench Audio, 81.13 on Speech-BFCL and a 65.51% task success rate on τ-Voice at 1.91s mean latency in thinking mode, plus 51.27% English EVA accuracy. It puts reasoning and tool calling in the same open model as speech, where [[2026-09-25#2|Google's Gemini 3.8 TTS models]] were generation-only and closed.
items.title: ServiceNow releases Apriel Voice 27B Preview, an open speech model with tool use

items.summary: An asynchronous runtime that splits a slow planner from fast policies and routes each step to one of a pool. Over 3,000 test episodes on 60 LIBERO-Pro tasks it reaches 95.9% success against 94.7% for the best single policy in its own pool, using 25% fewer control steps and 17% less control time; on 100 RoboTwin 2.0 episodes it scores 84% with VLA policies and 86% with VLA plus code, against 80% for the strongest single baseline, and it transfers to BEHAVIOR-1K and a real Unitree G1.
items.title: REA routes between robot policies and cuts control steps 25% at higher success

items.summary: SimpleLoRIF backpropagates only through the final four transformer blocks, making gradient attribution feasible on datasets of about a million examples; it separates misaligned models' unsafe responses with AUC up to 0.865. Removing the 20% of Tulu 3 most gradient-aligned with unsafe responses cuts GCG attack success by up to 22% across Qwen, Llama and Olmo with capability largely preserved. It attacks at the data level what [[2026-10-31#2|OpenAI's monitoring stack]] and [[2026-11-01#1|Anthropic's own defeated monitor]] address at inference time.
items.title: Follow the Gradient traces unsafe behaviour back to the training examples that caused it

items.summary: A NeurIPS 2026 paper that replaces discrete chain-of-thought with reasoning in continuous latent space for unified multimodal models, trained by curriculum supervised fine-tuning then information-gain reinforcement learning. It reports state of the art on GenEval with a 7-percentage-point gain over BAGEL, and test-time scaling gains over token-based generation under both parallel and sequential strategies.
items.title: LARC reasons in continuous latent space and gains 7 points on GenEval

2026-11-03.lead: SemiAnalysis published GDPx, an agentic benchmark across eleven high-value domains on which the best model, Claude Opus 5.5, scores 12% and every model scores zero on the finance and legal tasks.
2026-11-03.window: 2 Nov 07:00 → 3 Nov 07:00 JST (+ late catches from 27–30 Oct)

items.summary: The amended filing says this is "one of the areas covered by our Responsible Scaling Policy, which sets out our plans to monitor and mitigate the risks as we approach what has been termed 'recursive self-improvement'", and that internal estimates indicate Anthropic may imminently satisfy the policy's definition of "dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI". No current model has been designated as past that threshold, Anthropic says it does not expect to safely let Claude design successive frontier generations without meaningful human supervision, and it is considering RSP updates to keep humans in control. The same filing reports Q3 revenue of about $17B against a $23.29B net loss and roughly $895.4B of purchase commitments and leases. It follows [[2026-10-28#1|the S-1's disclosure of a month-long training pause]].
items.title: Anthropic tells the SEC its recursive self-improvement threshold may be imminent

items.summary: SJTU's DENG Lab co-designs generation, training and execution so that multi-step denoising yields one output chunk per concurrent forward round, with chunk-wise causal attention, staggered denoising across model replicas and a Wave Parallelism runtime that delivers K/V early. On Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B, 4-step Wave Forcing reaches 147.6 DiT FPS and 134.8 end-to-end FPS — 7.07x single-GPU throughput — and the DiT-only tests show up to 2.53x the best context-parallel baseline across 1.3B–14B models; on 100-second videos Dynamic Degree rises from 36.63 to 91.45. It pushes on the real-time generation frontier opened by [[2026-10-29#1|Genie 4]].
items.title: Wave Forcing streams long video at 134.8 end-to-end FPS on eight H200s

items.summary: A nested double-loop framework: an outer world-data-model flywheel aims data construction at the model's measured weaknesses, while an inner loop mines workflows from instructional videos by dual-path trajectory reconstruction and propagates them into reusable primitives for verifiable synthetic tasks, with snapshot-rollback retries during real-environment collection. The 27B model reports 80.2 on OSWorld-Verified, 36.9 on OSWorld 2.0, 43.9 on WeaveBench and 25.0 on Agents' Last Exam, with gains compounding across recursive iterations. Another route into desktop control after [[2026-11-02#4|Vercel's agent-desktop]].
items.title: CUA-Master-27B scores 80.2 on OSWorld-Verified from recursively mined workflows

items.summary: The all-stock deal values Lumentum at about $1,132 a share, a 23.9% premium to the 28 October close, leaves Marvell holders with 67% of the combined company and targets completion in the first half of 2028. It bets on optical interconnect as the data-centre bottleneck; both stocks fell on the announcement.
items.title: Marvell to buy Lumentum for $115B in the largest public tech merger on record

items.summary: The benchmark covers caregiving, health, education, household admin, finances, shopping and government services, with the task set derived from the American Time Use Survey, the Multinational Time Use Study and a 3,995-respondent survey. GPT-6 Astra averages 80.6% reward against 80.0% for GPT-5.6 and 49.3% for GPT-5.2 under nine months earlier; the full task set and grading method are not released. It is a flattering counterpart to [[2026-11-03#0|GDPx, where the best model scored 12% on professional work]] — the gap between errands and expert labour, measured twice in two days.
items.title: OpenAI's LifeVal puts GPT-6 Astra at 80.6% on everyday errands

items.summary: Renmin University's harness lets the model decide actions, delegation and acceptance while a runtime holds state and feedback, with a three-layer architecture for synchronous or asynchronous subagents, a shared application layer where humans and agents edit the same documents, CAD models and Blender scenes, and persistent semantic memory. It reports being competitive with Codex and the DeepSeek harness across 12 benchmarks and 6 application categories; using GLM-5.3 to post-train Qwen3.6-35B-A3B over five rounds lifted the eight-benchmark average from 33.19 to 42.95. A third recursive-self-improvement harness in a week after [[2026-11-01#6|Xiaomi's A-RSI]] and [[2026-10-29#5|The Trinity]] — and the research version of the threshold Anthropic flagged above.
items.title: CoworkOS splits agent strategy from execution and self-improves a 35B model

items.summary: 240 tasks across 8 teamwork dimensions, each drawn from a real record — aviation accident reports, clinical cases, coding tasks, negotiations — with programmatically verifiable outcomes, and models scored only on tasks they can already solve alone. Across 18 closed and open-weight models every one shows clear teamwork weaknesses: frontier models refuse unsafe shortcuts and report misconduct but reach the best available deal in just 14% of conflicts, and their pass rate falls from 97% to 81% when inheriting a task a weaker model cheated on. Models of near-identical general capability differ by up to 11 points as teammates; 160 tasks are public and 80 held out.
items.title: Stanford's teamwork benchmark: best model 82.2/100, best deal in 14% of conflicts

items.summary: CMU freezes a literature snapshot at 2025, has six models write research proposals, then scores them against what the same communities actually published in 2026 — over 90,000 proposals across four areas. Agent populations cite as diversely as a human community and cover its tasks and methods, but rarely land on the concrete approaches it pursues, and neither richer field context nor larger populations closes the gap; blinded expert review puts AI proposals closest to real papers on presentation and furthest on expected success. It measures from the generation side what [[2026-11-01#4|OpenFrontiers measured from the rediscovery side]].
items.title: IdeaTaste: research agents reach 26% of human citation taste and 18% on ideas

items.summary: A family of MXFP8 and mixed NVFP4/FP8 attention kernels that reuse quantized operands across matrix orientations via token-block scaling, guard against scale-induced causal leakage, and keep forward and backward numerics consistent while handling variable-length packed documents without repacking. On causal packed-document workloads the MXFP8 path speeds the combined forward-and-backward attention call, quantization included, by 1.10–1.40x on B200 and 1.06–1.42x on B300 over the fastest baseline per workload, validated on Llama-style pretraining.
items.title: Yandex's FLAMIA attention kernels cut Blackwell training time 1.10–1.42x

2026-11-04.lead: In an amended S-1, Anthropic told the SEC its internal estimates indicate it may imminently meet its Responsible Scaling Policy definition of dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI — the policy's recursive self-improvement threshold.

items.summary: A zkSNARK prototype proves a response came from the claimed model without revealing its weights, demonstrated on Llama 4 Maverick (400B MoE, 4-bit): 110 tokens per second of proving on one H100, about 19 MB per 1,024-token request, at 70–95x vLLM's GPU cost, with client verification in roughly 17 seconds. It proves an integer model under greedy decoding only, caps context at 1,024 tokens and hides weights but not architecture; code is Apache-2.0 and ships with Lean proofs.
items.title: Anthropic open-sources FlashProve, cryptographic proof that a 400B model served a reply

items.summary: Two engineers had the model produce the enclosure, circuit board and firmware for a device that interacts with Codex, with a contract manufacturer building a small batch of prototypes in under a month; several revisions were needed where Astra missed manufacturing constraints. OpenAI also reports BenchCAD 2.0, a benchmark for reconstructing 3D parts and assemblies on which an internal model averages 0.875, and 23-fold growth in internal hardware-team usage since February.
items.title: OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra designed a working Codex companion device in under a week

items.summary: An autonomous search over both algorithms and systems raises single-request speedup over autoregressive decoding from a stock 4.46x to 10.87x, and batched speedup from 1.94x to 3.93x, across four target models, three drafters, two GPU platforms and five benchmarks, with no training and no quality loss. It turns the compute accounting of [[2026-11-03#2|the predict-gate-execute analysis]] into an automatically tuned system.
items.title: SpecPilot discovers speculative-decoding algorithms, lifting speedup from 4.46x to 10.87x

items.summary: A pretrained video diffusion model is repurposed as a universal latent action learner, compressing each latent video frame from 1,200 tokens to 4. The authors report state-of-the-art results among latent action models on LARY-Bench, plus zero-shot cross-embodiment action transfer and cheaper downstream policy learning.
items.title: DreamX turns a video diffusion model into a latent action learner at 300x compression

items.summary: Q3 revenue of $13.4B with data center up 96.9% to $8.55B, a record quarter, and a raised 2027 growth outlook; MI450 Helios racks are in initial operation. Lisa Su said OpenAI chose EPYC Turin CPUs to host its first custom accelerator platforms, and more than 240 platforms are committed to the next-generation EPYC Venice. It prices the same AI build-out cycle as [[2026-11-04#3|the Marvell–Lumentum merger]].
items.title: AMD data center revenue nearly doubles to $8.5B; OpenAI picks EPYC Turin for its own chips

items.summary: A trajectory matrix of 374,401 scored runs over 452 candidate configurations and 25 benchmarks puts per-input oracle routing 5.4 points above the best single candidate. Learned routers recover 0.3 points across 16 benchmarks, 2.1 on video generation and 1.1 on robot manipulation while using 24% less policy time, and routing raises efficiency 8.82x on average over the reference model.
items.title: Route Anything: per-input oracle routing beats the best fixed model by 5.4 points

items.summary: Harder synthesised versions of AutomationBench and tau3-Bench Banking drop seven frontier models by up to 38.2 points; training on the generated environments raises Qwen3.6-35B-A3B from 23.0 to 41.0 average across seven long-horizon tool-use benchmarks (43.2 with RL) and GLM-5.2 from 44.6 to 56.6. It applies the task-synthesis route of [[2026-11-02#3|WorkFactory]] to tool environments rather than occupations.
items.title: ToolSpace synthesises tool environments and lifts GLM-5.2 to 56.6, Claude Opus 5 level

items.summary: The system learns a domain from its own experience, storing skills and reflections in a knowledge repository instead of relying on human experts or a stronger teacher: held-out all-pass rate on Harvey's LAB Firm Knowledge rises from 30.0% to 55.0% with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and from 35.0% to 46.0% with Qwen3.8-Flash. It is the research-side counterpart to [[2026-11-04#0|Anthropic's recursive self-improvement warning to the SEC]] and to [[2026-11-01#6|Xiaomi's A-RSI]].
items.title: Alibaba's Recursa self-improves into new domains with no teacher: 30% to 55% on legal

items.summary: A 31-page technical report argues later tokens cost up to 7x more than earlier ones on frontier open-weight models, that frequent context compaction costs little to no task accuracy on long-horizon and long-input work, and that performance does not collapse on long-horizon SWE tasks even at one action per context. It proposes semantic state space models as the alternative to extending windows.
items.title: "You don't need long context": compaction matches long-context runs on SWE tasks

2026-11-05.lead: Anthropic open-sourced FlashProve, a prototype that cryptographically proves a response came from the model a provider claims to have used, running at 110 tokens per second on a single H100 against a 400B-parameter model.

sources.label: OpenAI — A thousand fewer paths to root

items.summary: The pipeline scanned about 2.8M lines of a stock Linux kernel, produced 2,308 deduplicated candidate findings in 12 hours, reproduced 1,724 of them in 30 hours and built working local privilege-escalation exploits for 948, plus candidate patches; total API cost was $1,213,430, about $1,279 per unique vulnerability. A July run with GPT-5.6 Sol had found 166. Maintainers had patched 61 upstream when the work concluded, with 43 more in preparation.
items.title: OpenAI's autonomous pipeline builds 948 working Linux root exploits in one run

sources.label: Anthropic — Investigating vault particles with Claude

items.summary: Searching about 15 billion predicted proteins surfaced vault relatives in 29 bacterial and 4 archaeal phyla, present in under 1% of sequenced genomes; of 44 candidates tested cell-free, 15 of 24 gave soluble protein, 7 of those 15 formed vault-like particles and cryo-EM confirmed 4. The L05 phage vault is 96 copies of a single protein (~9.5 MDa, ~54x45 nm) against 78 copies and 67x40 nm in mammals, enclosing about 25% more volume, and purification fell from ~3 days to ~90 minutes. A second phage-biology result from Anthropic's lab after [[2026-09-24#0|the ART enzyme system]], and the first from the expanded programme in [[2026-10-31#9|AI for Science]].
items.title: Claude helps determine the first structure of a vault particle outside eukaryotes

items.summary: An open-weight multimodal agentic MoE with 93 layers and 896 experts (16 routed plus 2 shared), a 401M MoonViT-V2 vision encoder and MXFP4 quantization-aware training; self-reported scores include 65.7 on Terminal-Bench 4.0, 79.6 on OSWorld V2.1, 94.2 on GPQA-Diamond and 92.1 on BrowseComp. It ships under a bespoke Kimi K3.1 Pro licence rather than Apache 2.0, continuing the pattern in [[2026-09-28#2|Chinese open-weight token share]].
items.title: Moonshot ships Kimi K3.1 Pro: 2.8T parameters, 104B active, 1M context

items.summary: A 65B dense transformer pretrained on 12T tokens, released under Apache 2.0 with up to 1M context; in-house evals report 80.5 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 76.5 on SWE-bench Verified, 61.4 on SWE-bench Pro v1.0 and 85.2 on GPQA-Diamond, with training cost put at about $32M. It claims to edge out [[2026-10-07#1|Reflection AI's 501B Beam]] at 80.1 with one eighth the parameters.
items.title: Ricursive's Ripple-65B Preview: a 65B dense model at 80.5 on Terminal-Bench 2.1

items.summary: Gemini 3.8 Flash, Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna fall to 13% accuracy or lower on the longest problems of the hardest 'General finite' level. Trained from scratch at 275M parameters, Gated DeltaNet and hybrid models stayed near perfect out to about 10x their training length (trained to 256 assignments, tested to 64,000), while transformers never learned the hardest level at all — an architectural result, not a scale one. It cuts against the context-length framing in [[2026-11-05#8|yesterday's compaction paper]].
items.title: Ai2's StateBench: frontier models drop to 13% tracking state over long documents

items.summary: 56 end-to-end physics research tasks built by 42 physicists across nine domains, graded by deterministic verifiers plus expert rubrics; across 22 models in 26 configurations the best passes 46 of 168 rollouts, with failures traced to insufficiently rigorous reasoning and limited expert intuition. A second hard ceiling on research agents after [[2026-11-01#4|OpenFrontiers]].
items.title: FrontierPhysics: no model configuration passes more than 46 of its 168 rollouts

items.summary: Image generation runs up to 50% faster and can now produce animated GIFs from text or photos, with GPT-Image-2.6 Flare and Sunburst added to the API; OpenAI puts current output at more than 4 billion images per week.
items.title: ChatGPT Images 2.6 adds animated GIFs and two API image models

items.summary: Advisory XSA-523 covers CVE-2026-102703 and CVE-2026-102704, a grant-copy defect letting one malicious guest read and write any other guest's memory; every Xen release from 4.6 onward is affected (4.5 and earlier are safe), including all supported Qubes releases. Discovery is credited to Claude, the same week as the OpenAI kernel run above and following [[2026-10-07#2|Anthropic's three-tier cyber programme]].
items.title: Xen credits Claude for two critical grant-copy VM-escape flaws

items.summary: CNBC reports every data-centre ballot measure across ten states went against the projects bar one, with Ohio alone restricting or banning them in 14 municipalities; Goldman Sachs estimates the state and local results could trigger moratoria covering about 45% of planned US capacity expansion, and Hut 8 fell 23% and IREN 11%. It turns the local resistance behind [[2026-09-22#3|$68B of blocked projects]] into a nationwide electoral result.
items.title: US voters reject data centres in all but one ballot measure of the midterms

items.summary: An encoder-free, native VLA framework that maps pixels to actions in one model; under controlled comparisons native architectures beat encoder-based counterparts, and full fine-tuning of the encoder-based baselines narrows but does not close the gap. The day's most-upvoted paper on Hugging Face, with no benchmark numbers in the abstract.
items.title: NEO-VLA argues vision-language-action policies should drop the vision encoder

items.summary: On Qwen3 models, OPD and MOPD reach 96.04–102.73% of their teachers' in-distribution scores while their out-of-distribution scores stay 2.45–16.25% below the base model's, and compositional OOD performance runs 18.19–24.34% below the best teachers. Consolidating RL gains by distillation trades away the breadth it was meant to preserve.
items.title: On-policy distillation recovers teacher scores in-distribution but loses generalisation

items.summary: The paper separates the two with a Pass@(K,T) metric over sampling breadth K and interaction depth T, finding multi-turn RL's gains concentrated in depth, and proposes BudgetMix RL, which varies the interaction budget during training rather than fixing it.
items.title: Multi-turn RL buys interaction depth, not sampling breadth

items.summary: Native clip length rises from 10 to 15 seconds, settable in 1-second steps from 3, with multi-turn conversational editing, better reference adherence and 1080p or 4K upscaling; pricing drops 30% to $0.07 per second of 720p video, generally available on the Gemini API and Google Cloud with SynthID watermarks.
items.title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generates 15-second clips at 30% lower cost

2026-11-06.lead: An autonomous OpenAI pipeline found 2,308 candidate flaws in the Linux kernel and built 948 working local root exploits in a single 30-hour run, at about $1,279 per unique vulnerability.
2026-11-06.window: 5 Nov 07:00 → 6 Nov 07:00 JST (+ late catches from 3 Nov)

items.summary: The security-research model scores 48.5% on ExploitGym, which turns known vulnerabilities into working exploits, against 32.1% for GPT-5.6 Cyber, and OpenAI reports it avoids out-of-scope services 99.93% of the time without deployment safety prompts (94.49% for its predecessor). It is Critical under the Preparedness Framework and available only via the API and Codex to selected Daybreak Red customers; OpenAI credits it with the 948 Linux privilege-escalation exploits of [[2026-11-06#0|yesterday's pipeline]] and 81 previously unknown high-severity Firefox flaws.
items.title: OpenAI ships GPT-6 Cyber, its first model rated Critical for cybersecurity

items.summary: Instead of emitting coordinates one token at a time, VFlash predicts points, boxes and trajectories jointly with a lightweight drafter in a single forward pass, measuring about 25x faster generation on 3D point motion forecasting in a single-rollout test. A world action model conditioned on its plans reaches 70.2% average success across four MolmoSpaces task suites against 62.6% for the baseline — the opposite bet to [[2026-11-06#9|NEO-VLA's case for dropping the vision encoder]], keeping the perception stack and attacking the decoding cost instead.
items.title: NVIDIA's VFlash decodes visual primitives in one pass, ~25x faster than token-by-token

items.summary: The Nasdaq fell 5.2% intraday on 5 November and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped about 9.75%, on track for its steepest daily loss since March 2020; AMD and Micron each lost roughly 15%, Qualcomm 11.2%, Arm 11% and Nvidia almost 9%. The trigger is the moratorium risk behind [[2026-11-06#8|the 41 data-centre ballot measures voters passed]] — Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa wants an immediate moratorium, and Wells Fargo puts 27% of planned US data-centre gigawatts in Texas.
items.title: Chip and AI stocks lose about $3T as data-centre ballot results sink in

items.summary: DOJ-SITF, led by Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward and Associate Deputy Attorney General Stephen Weiss, will prosecute misuse of SI by foreign and state-sponsored actors, transnational criminal organisations and corporate actors, with Attorney General Todd Blanche naming attacks on taxpayers, critical infrastructure and national security. It is the first dedicated US federal enforcement body for AI misuse and adopts the 'super intelligence' vocabulary of [[2026-09-28#0|the US–China dialogue agreed at the Trump–Xi summit]].
items.title: US Justice Department launches a Super Intelligence Task Force

items.summary: ByteDance Seed researchers train a sparse autoencoder on an MoE layer's output and decompose each latent's pre-activation exactly across experts, on layers 4, 30 and 46 of Qwen3-30B-A3B. Contribution is more concentrated than the gating weights suggest, most latents have one or two dominant experts, and auto-interpretation finds distinctions as fine as separate experts for Java and front-end web code, or geometry versus arithmetic; the SAEs and code are released.
items.title: Sparse autoencoders show MoE experts specialise in human-readable ways

items.summary: Conductor's product orchestrates multiple AI coding agents in parallel on one codebase; Meta is folding the team into its software-engineering work and terms were not disclosed. It is the second multi-agent coding tool to change hands or open up in a week, after [[2026-11-02#10|DeepSeek open-sourcing Super-Agent]].
items.title: Meta acquires Conductor, whose app runs several coding agents at once

2026-11-07.lead: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber, the first model it has classified as Critical for cybersecurity under its Preparedness Framework, and is restricting it to selected Daybreak Red customers.
2026-11-07.window: 6 Nov 07:00 → 7 Nov 07:00 JST (+ late catch from 4 Nov)

items.summary: The conjecture, stated by Scott Aaronson in a 2008 lecture, asked whether any quantum query algorithm has at least one input bit with measurable influence; the proof gives a classical deterministic approximation of a quantum algorithm's acceptance probability on all but a small fraction of uniformly random inputs, with classical query count growing as a fixed power of the quantum one. A research system built and run by David Turturean at Physical Superintelligence (PSI) produced the first complete proof during the third day of a run, then two improvements to the bound; all three were formalised and kernel-checked in Lean. Stanford's Guy Blanc, Jordan Docter, Carmen Strassle and Li-Yang Tan, who proved a narrower result in August 2026, are reading the full proof. It bounds input reads only, not total computation time. A second AI-assisted scientific result in three days after [[2026-11-06#1|Claude's vault-particle structure]].
items.title: Unreleased Anthropic model proves the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, checked in Lean

items.summary: Human-guided agents produced two results: RSA padding gives far less protection than assumed once an attacker controls about half the signed block, and for the harder 32-byte-fingerprint case a new algorithm improves on the best known method by roughly 1,600x for 1024-bit keys on DeepMind's theoretical estimates; separately, a batch-factoring algorithm with better asymptotic complexity than any prior one cuts the marginal cost of each additional 1024-bit key by about 30x. In a sandbox against an already-solved 1024-bit benchmark key the agents reproduced the padding attack with 3.5x less CPU time; no live key was factored and 2048-bit keys are reported unaffected. Dj Dvijotham and Abhradeep Thakurta led the work with Nadia Heninger (UC San Diego, Inria) and Emmanuel Thomé (Inria). It extends the week's run of AI-found security results after [[2026-11-07#0|GPT-6 Cyber]] and [[2026-11-06#7|the Xen VM-escape flaws credited to Claude]].
items.title: DeepMind's agents find two new weaknesses in legacy 1024-bit RSA

items.summary: Four open models (8B, 9B, 35B with 3B active, and a vision-tuned 27B 'Max') return a probability distribution over user-supplied options without autoregressive decoding, trained with supervised fine-tuning plus reinforcement learning from adjusted feedback. Max scores 67.52 against 60.70 for Jev 1.14.0 on the public Decision Index 0.4.1 suite, is statistically tied with d3-turbo and GPT-6 Sol on Decision Bench v4 while trailing Claude Opus 5.5 by 1.6 points, and answers in 183 ms against about 2.0 s for GPT-6 Sol and 3.5 s for Claude Opus 5.5.
items.title: Drex: open non-autoregressive decision models answer in 183 ms and match GPT-6 Sol

items.summary: A fully open recipe for pretraining embodied foundation models on human video reports a log-linear scaling law between egocentric pretraining hours and robot success rate, using a 50,000-hour dataset. A world-action model pretrained on human video alone reaches 92.08% success on RoboTwin 2.0 Clean2Clean and 68.88% on Clean2Random, and 14.17% mean success on RoboDojo; the goal-conditioned variant reaches 92.70% and 84.60%. A different bet from [[2026-11-06#9|NEO-VLA's argument for dropping the vision encoder]].
items.title: Open-HumanScale: 50,000 hours of egocentric video, and a scaling law to robot success

items.summary: A unified model handling text-to-image generation, instruction-guided editing and multi-reference synthesis in one interleaved sequence: 31.7B stored parameters with about 5.4B activated per target latent token via a Mixture-of-Transformers plus MoE, trained natively at 1.5K resolution. The authors report the 1536-resolution model ranks first among the open-source models they evaluated on PRISM-Bench, Qwen-Image-Bench and UnicBench, without giving per-benchmark scores, and a MeanFlow-distilled Turbo variant renders 1024x1024 in 4.98 s on a single NVIDIA H20 using eight guidance-free steps. It is built for single-GPU deployment inside WeChat.
items.title: WeChat's WeLM-Image: 31.7B MoE image model, 1024x1024 in 4.98 s on one H20

items.summary: The 'National Community Compact' and an accompanying Compute Campus Policy Blueprint commit OpenAI to limiting nondisclosure agreements with public officials, covering the electricity and energy-infrastructure costs of data centres it owns and operates, publishing construction plans and noise levels, writing per-community water-use plans, and investing in local childcare, education, healthcare and transport. No dollar amounts or volumes were given, and the power commitment covers only owned-and-operated sites. It came two days after the midterms, in which [[2026-11-06#8|voters rejected data centres in all but one ballot measure]], and before [[2026-11-07#2|the roughly $3T selloff in chip and AI stocks]].
items.title: OpenAI limits data-centre NDAs and will cover power costs after ballot defeats

2026-11-08.lead: Physical Superintelligence says a non-public Anthropic model found a proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, open since 2008, on the third day of a run, and the main theorem was formalised and kernel-checked in Lean.
2026-11-08.window: 7 Nov 07:00 → 8 Nov 07:00 JST (+ late catches from 4–6 Nov; no arXiv listing and no Hugging Face Daily Papers page published for 7 Nov)

items.summary: Moonshot AI's TCSExam has 100 expert-reviewed tasks (theorem proving, solver engineering, constructions, open conjectures), each checked by the Lean kernel or an executable checker, plus a 20-task Lite subset that cuts attempts 80% and ranks agents almost identically (Spearman rho 0.93). GPT-6 Astra leads Full with index 71.9 and Opus 5.5 leads Lite with 72.3; on the 30 open-conjecture tasks Kimi K3 built a 124-vertex graph with 630 edges and no triangles or 4-cycles, beating the 629-edge construction of Goedgebeur et al. (2025), and GPT-6 Astra built a [[25,7,6]] quantum code, one better in distance than the [[25,7,5]] entry in Grassl's tables. It sharpens the week's AI-does-real-mathematics thread behind [[2026-11-08#0|the Aaronson-Ambainis proof]] and [[2026-11-08#1|DeepMind's RSA findings]], while showing that nonzero conjecture scores partly reused already-published counterexamples.
items.title: TCSExam: frontier agents score ~72 on TCS research and set two new combinatorial records

items.summary: Agent-R2 synthesises 4k agent training tasks from 10k real web-corpus candidates, keeping real attachments and deliverable-level rubrics, then trains a 4B model with SFT plus rubric-based RL. It reaches 51.0% on GDPval against 48.0% for Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507, and 14.8% vs 13.8% on OfficeQA, the same real-source-synthesis bet as [[2026-11-02#3|WorkFactory]] measured on the kind of economically grounded work [[2026-11-03#0|GDPx]] probes.
items.title: Agent-R2: a 4B agent scores 51.0% on GDPval, above Qwen3-235B's 48.0%

items.summary: StrataFlux recovers accuracy lost to 2-4-bit weight and 2-3-bit KV-cache quantisation by streaming higher-precision data out of host RAM and SSDs instead of GPU memory. Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct at 2-bit goes from 9.46 to 8.40 WikiText-2 perplexity while keeping 95.4% of the quantised model's throughput on an RTX 5090, and at 128K context a 3-bit/2-bit configuration matches vLLM's 4-bit AWQ with 8-bit KV on perplexity and speed using about half the GPU memory.
items.title: StrataFlux lifts 2-bit Qwen3-8B from 11.0% to 47.1% on AIME by streaming from host RAM

items.summary: Measuring accuracy per training FLOP, this study finds on-policy distillation loses to GRPO with an external teacher but needs 50x fewer distillation FLOPs for the same maths accuracy when the teacher is the student's own GRPO checkpoint; a two-domain pipeline matches joint GRPO with 42.0% fewer total FLOPs, and multi-teacher distillation costs 5.2% (2 domains) to 8.0% (4 domains) of specialist training. It puts a compute price on the generalisation gap reported in [[2026-11-06#10|on-policy distillation]].
items.title: On-policy distillation beats GRPO only with the student's own GRPO checkpoint as teacher

items.summary: A committee of independent directors with outside counsel will examine reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort; the board says it has no reason to believe national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised and retains confidence in Huang, who has committed to cooperating. The review opens nine days before NVIDIA's quarterly results, and House committee chairs have separately asked Huang to brief them on 18 November.
items.title: NVIDIA board opens independent probe into a foreign intelligence effort on Jensen Huang

sources.label: Sell The News (source timeline, FT first)

items.summary: The Financial Times reports Anthropic committed about $3.4bn to roughly 1.7 GW of heavy-duty gas-fired generators, taking over Caterpillar orders that San Antonio supplier OnePWR Solutions placed around two years ago plus engineering and construction capacity; the deal was finalised in late September and is not an acquisition of OnePWR. It would be the largest known single purchase of power-generation equipment by an AI lab, and it lands while [[2026-11-06#8|US voters are rejecting data centres at the ballot box]] and [[2026-11-08#5|OpenAI is promising to cover power costs]]. Bloomberg and Reuters both attribute the story to the FT, so it rests on one original source.
items.title: Anthropic reportedly pays $3.4bn for 1.7 GW of gas generators via OnePWR

items.summary: SwarmEvolve runs LLM-guided evolutionary search with agent swarms that reason in latent space, share KV caches and are filtered for novelty on hidden states. It takes the highest average score across 21 problems and needs a median 3 to 8 minutes to reach scores other frameworks need 60 minutes for, and with Qwen3 8B it improves on some AlphaEvolve solutions, extending the automated-discovery line of [[2026-11-05#2|SpecPilot]].
items.title: SwarmEvolve: latent agent swarms hit rivals' 60-minute best scores in 3-8 minutes

2026-11-09.lead: Moonshot AI's TCSExam benchmarks frontier agents across the whole of theoretical computer science research, and its open-conjecture track produced two independently checked new records: a 124-vertex, 630-edge triangle- and C4-free graph and a [[25,7,6]] quantum code.
2026-11-09.selection: papers-v2 (paper threshold 5, press threshold 6; quiet-day exception used for two press items at 5)
2026-11-09.window: 8 Nov 07:00 → 9 Nov 07:00 JST (+ late catches from 5 Nov; weekend, so no new arXiv announcement day or Hugging Face Daily Papers page after Fri 6 Nov)

items.summary: The agent writes and executes code to build a dynamic 3D scene — a "Draft Video" — whose structure and motion then condition a downstream video generator; it is trained by supervised fine-tuning on 6k trajectories followed by agentic RL on 2k with dual execution and video rewards. Against its base generator it reports roughly +7 points on PhyGenBench and +24 on VBench-2.0.
items.title: Video-Coder writes code to stage 3D scenes, lifting VBench-2.0 by about 24 points

items.summary: Running 16 weight-editing trajectories on Qwen3.5-0.8B and Qwen3.5-9B across seven benchmarks, the authors report held-out gains of up to 29.45 points on MATH-500 (from editing 1,023 parameters), 36.72 on IFEval, 17.11 on SciBench and 4.42 on GPQA Diamond; a math-edited checkpoint then improves GPQA Diamond, IFEval and SciBench by 3.03, 12.18 and 20.10 points with no further editing, while 6 of 16 trajectories reverted to the original weights when no edit could be validated. It is the first systematic test of the limits of the weight editing [[2026-11-03#1|GPT-6 Astra demonstrated last week]], and the transfer result is new.
items.title: A math edit of 1,023 parameters transfers to benchmarks it was not edited for

items.summary: The Authorization Drift Benchmark puts 648 samples across seven domains to 13 models and three frameworks over 25,207 trajectories, and finds frontier-capable models drift at rates of 0.43 to 0.61 — higher than weaker ones — while 86.18% of tasks still admit a clean-success trajectory, so the drift is avoidable. Most of it is early over-collection of data; mapped to four jurisdictions, data minimisation is the provision most often implicated and 93.5% of legally grounded drifting runs breach more than one. It is the first measurement of the permission-overstepping that [[2026-09-25#1|Transluce documented in the wild]].
items.title: Authorization Drift: more capable agents overstep their permissions more often

items.summary: TPU 8tx reuses TPU 8t silicon with 5th Gen AMD EPYC hosts for confidential inference, claiming up to 2x lower latency than TPU 8t at near-zero security overhead and supporting private fine-tuning, distillation and RL in one system; TPU 8i Max packages two TPU 8i chips together for double the compute, SRAM and HBM bandwidth in the same rack footprint, aimed at very long context windows. The two complete an eighth-generation family of four, and Google gives no dates, regions or named customers.
items.title: Google adds TPU 8tx for confidential inference and a dual-chip TPU 8i Max

items.summary: In a post-midterm 60 Minutes interview Trump said AI risks "can be managed", named the Justice Department as the manager, and said he does not mind guardrails provided the US is not left in a "deep second position" to China, adding he could work with Democrats on them. It is a shift from the position the White House took at the UN in September, and follows [[2026-11-06#8|the data-centre defeats in the midterm ballot measures]] and [[2026-11-07#3|the DOJ's new Super Intelligence Task Force]].
items.title: Trump says AI risks can be managed and signals openness to guardrails

items.summary: The Ulanqab site is planned for up to 800MW of IT capacity across four built-to-suit phases for two unnamed internet giants, with a first 120MW phase delivered in August 2026 at about a fifth of US costs and completion expected by end of 2027; Envision aims to supply over 60% of the first two phases' 240MW load from 420MW of its own wind farms, and runs a 5MW pilot hall converting 10kV AC straight to 800V DC at the rack. SemiAnalysis compares it directly with Stargate Abilene (~820MW), and reports Chinese rents roughly halved over five years to about $40/kW/month excluding power. It is the site-level sequel to [[2026-09-27#4|their China datacenter model]].
items.title: SemiAnalysis visits Envision's 800MW Galaxy campus in Inner Mongolia

2026-11-10.lead: Video-Coder has a coding agent write and run code to stage a rough 3D scene, then feeds that structure to a video generator, gaining about 24 points on VBench-2.0 over the generator alone.
2026-11-10.selection: papers-v2 (paper threshold 6 from a 0.67 seven-day paper share, press threshold 6; quiet-day exception used for two press items at 5)
2026-11-10.window: 9 Nov 07:00 → 10 Nov 07:00 JST (+ late catches from 6–7 Nov; Monday's arXiv announcement carried Friday's submissions, so nothing in the paper lane is newer than 6 Nov)

items.summary: One underlying model under two access regimes: Fable 5.2 is generally available with cyber and biology safeguards, Mythos 5.2 only to organizations vetted through the Cyber and Life Sciences programs. Anthropic reports 49.1% on FrontierCode 2.0, 69.9 on FrontierSWE v2, 41.3% on the Remote Labor Index and 74.2 on Humanity's Last Exam with tools, plus a Fermat's Last Theorem formalization in 30 hours by about 1,000 Fable 5.2 agents where Opus 5.5 reached 26% in 18 hours; Mythos 5.2 hits 89.6 on internal CVE Rediscovery, 10.2% above Opus 5.5 ([[2026-09-23#0|Opus 5.5]]). The gated-access pattern follows OpenAI's Critical-rated cyber model ([[2026-11-07#0]]).
items.title: Anthropic ships Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 at $8/$40 per 1M tokens

items.summary: Google DeepMind's multi-LLM agent framework, powered by Gemini Carbon, wrote over six million lines of Lean in about four weeks to prove key security properties of Signal's actual cryptographic protocol implementation, with human reviewers reading only the ~1% of the codebase the agents flagged. Two previously fixed bugs reintroduced into an isolated copy were each caught with a machine-checked proof of insecurity; artifacts are open-sourced. Extends the Lean-verification thread ([[2026-11-08#0]]) and DeepMind's agentic cryptanalysis ([[2026-11-08#1]]).
items.title: AlphaProof Code formally verifies Signal's protocol code down to machine instructions

items.summary: A permissively licensed multimodal coding model reported at 88.4 on Terminal Bench v2.1, with API pricing of $0.30/$1.20 per 1M tokens, putting a near-frontier agentic coder into self-hostable hands. Continues the run of very large Chinese open-weight releases ([[2026-11-06#2|Kimi K3.1 Pro]]).
items.title: Meituan opens LongCat-2.5 weights under MIT: 1.6T MoE, ~48B active, 1M context

items.summary: Unveiled at CoRL 2026 and built on Cosmos-Predict2.5, GR00T 2 averages 71% success across 50 manipulation tasks with a single demonstration each and handles 40 of the 50 zero-shot; Isaac Lab 3.0 shipped alongside, with weights and dataset due in December. Lands in the same argument about how much visual machinery a VLA needs ([[2026-11-06#9|NEO-VLA]]).
items.title: NVIDIA GR00T 2: a 2B vision-language-action model at 71% success from one demo per task

items.summary: Google confirmed Gemini 4 Carbon is available via the Gemini API in AI Studio, with introductory pricing reported at $2/$10 per 1M tokens rising to $4/$20 after 30 November. On Google's own new MKA benchmark it ranks second in quality while costing roughly 6x less per task than the top-scoring model.
items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon reaches general availability in the Gemini API

items.summary: A metacognitive architecture for scientific discovery ranks first on all eight metrics of Taiyi-Bench (265 tasks drawn from 50 papers across ten disciplines), scoring 54.0 overall against 47.9 for AI Scientist-v2. Its chemistry optimization raised a cobalt-catalyzed carbonylation from trace yield to 84% and a photocatalytic allylic amination from 13% to 69%, which is wet-lab evidence rather than benchmark-only ([[2026-11-04#7|IdeaTaste]]).
items.title: Sage-Taiyi scores 54.0 on Taiyi-Bench and lifts two real catalytic reaction yields

items.summary: Trained only on RoboTwin Clean demonstrations, SWAM reaches 88.10% success on the Easy (Clean-to-Clean) split and 61.56% on Hard (Clean-to-Random), and across three real-world tasks scores 40.00% against 23.33% for the strongest baseline. Adds to the case that large passive video corpora transfer to robot policies ([[2026-11-08#3|Open-HumanScale]]).
items.title: SWAM: a world-action model on 47,000 hours of video nearly doubles real-world success

items.summary: A five-stage agentic workflow tunes training configurations against global execution-time and peak-memory models, delivering up to 2.75x speedup across four single- and multi-node dense and MoE LLM workloads and transferring experience across GPU types. The same self-improvement idea applied to the stack rather than the model ([[2026-11-05#2|SpecPilot]]).
items.title: InfraRSI self-improves training infrastructure, raising MFU from 17.4% to 30.0%

items.summary: A fail-closed central system tracks RL, evaluation, agentic sampling and data-processing workloads across OpenAI's research infrastructure and can halt model output within 35 seconds of an intervention decision; it does not cover ChatGPT or the public API. A concrete control layer behind the lab disclosures about recursive self-improvement timelines ([[2026-11-04#0]]).
items.title: OpenAI's Control Room can cut off a research model's output within 35 seconds

items.summary: An intrusion on 24 October through a compromised cloud provider reached billing records and, for some accounts, API secrets, customer datasets and incomplete model weights at an inference provider serving roughly 10,000 businesses; Notion separately confirmed Notion AI chat transcripts from under 1% of workspaces were exposed. It is the first major case of served model weights leaving a hosting provider, and a Hugging Face executive has already warned it may push open platforms to tighten access.
items.title: Fireworks AI breach exposed customer datasets, secrets and partial model weights

items.summary: On a 7B student, on-policy distillation holds its training quality at over 200x the numerical mismatch of a standard BF16 engine and only fails at about twice that, while two RL methods break at roughly 12x and 60x; within that budget FP8 KV caches hold at least 1.93x the tokens and FP8 with asynchronous rollouts reaches equal quality 1.62x sooner. A practical answer to the on-policy distillation question raised in [[2026-11-06#10]] and [[2026-11-09#3]].
items.title: On-policy distillation tolerates 200x more training-inference mismatch than RL

items.summary: MKA covers 10 verticals and 83 occupations with tasks that take a professional 3 to 8 hours, graded on ~70 yes/no checks weighted 75% factual accuracy and 25% visual design; the agentic autorater agreed with domain experts 96% of the time and models averaged 30 to 130 turns per task. Ten public tasks are on Hugging Face while the 200-task set stays private, a design meant to avoid the long-horizon collapse seen in [[2026-11-06#4|StateBench]].
items.title: Google and Artificial Analysis launch MKA, a 200-task visual knowledge-work benchmark

items.summary: A small model with a 1M-token context reported at 37.8% on AutomationBench-AA against 13.9% for Claude Haiku 5.5 and 20.2% for GPT-6 Luna, aimed at cheap high-throughput agent tasks. Another data point for small models punching above their size on agentic work ([[2026-11-09#1|Agent-R2]]).
items.title: Meta's Muse Ember targets high-volume agent work at $0.10/$0.50 per 1M tokens

items.summary: Announced at a San Francisco event: Claude Sheets in beta on all paid plans, Claude Meetings for Team and Enterprise joining Google Meet calls, Claude Whiteboards, Claude Data generally available, and plugins for Adobe, Atlassian and HubSpot. A move onto the productivity-suite surfaces rather than a model capability change.
items.title: Anthropic adds Claude Sheets, Meetings and Whiteboards; Claude Data hits GA

2026-11-11.lead: Anthropic shipped Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, one model under two access regimes, claiming the top score on most of its published frontier benchmarks and a 30-hour formalization of Fermat's Last Theorem by roughly 1,000 agents.

items.summary: The Lazarus method needs only write access to a checkpoint and inference-only compute: edited dormant neurons act as trigger detectors — the published example is the clock passing into 2027 — after which the agent downloads and runs attacker code with whatever access it holds, while passing standard safety evaluations. Microsoft says the attack was discovered by Claude Code with Opus 4.5, and that frontier agents can sometimes spot the anomalous weight edits but reliable detection requires diffing against the original weights.
items.title: Microsoft backdoors an AI agent by reprogramming fewer than 10 dormant neurons

items.summary: Trained on about 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein–ligand sequences at six scales from 42M to 1.6B parameters (a 1:2,000 parameter-to-token ratio), the model's frozen representations run five orders of magnitude faster than co-folding methods, and wet-lab validation across nine disease targets in seven protein families gives a 61.5% dose-response hit rate on de novo compounds. Accepted as a NeurIPS 2026 main-track oral, and a second route to AI-led discovery after [[2026-11-11#5|Sage-Taiyi]].
items.title: Bonbon: a protein–ligand foundation model with a 61.5% wet-lab hit rate on new compounds

items.summary: Recasting model repair as a bit-level Ising/QUBO problem instead of an LLM agent editing weights, Tree-Ising scores 54.6% on MATH-500 against the agent baseline's 51.7% and the base model's 7.9% (55.1% with a simulated-bifurcation solver), modifies 13–17% fewer weights, and needs four forward-pass requests, zero LLM tokens and roughly $0.90 of GPU time against the baseline's 158 agent turns and 89.7M tokens; on Qwen3.5-2B greedy GSM8K goes from 21.6% to 69.4%. A QAOA proof of concept ran on an IBM Heron processor. It is the optimisation-side answer to [[2026-11-10#1|the 1,023-parameter math edit]].
items.title: Tree-Ising repairs a broken model with bit-level Ising edits for about $0.90

items.summary: Under the state's AI safety law, developers above $500M in revenue must register with the new DIGIT office by 1 January 2027, publish safety frameworks and model transparency reports, and report critical incidents within 72 hours, with fines up to $1M for a first violation and $3M for repeats. Governor Hochul also announced a state evaluation programme, with a Binghamton University centre studying model risks under limited access to unreleased systems.

items.summary: A Business Hub lets companies claim verified profiles, update their information and see aggregate engagement, mention and click-through analytics, while eligible US e-commerce and online-service firms can deploy Business Agents that answer shopper questions and can be sponsored through ChatGPT Ads; Shopify merchants connect stores from the Shopify admin. It puts commercial agents in front of ChatGPT's roughly 1.2 billion weekly users.
items.title: OpenAI opens ChatGPT to verified business profiles and sponsored Business Agents

items.summary: Instead of updating weights, the method learns a binary mask over the gate projection and simply deletes weights; the trained mask is hundreds to thousands of times smaller than a full fine-tuning checkpoint. Under reinforcement learning, full fine-tuning, LoRA and random sparse fine-tuning each lose up to 5.4 points of prior-task accuracy where deletion does not. NeurIPS 2026, and a third result this week pointing at very sparse weight edits alongside [[2026-11-10#1|the 1,023-parameter math edit]].
items.title: Deletion Tuning: zeroing under 0.05% of weights matches full fine-tuning

items.summary: The benchmark runs 5,448 questions across 16 task categories, with option spaces from 2 to 1,024 and inputs up to 64,817 tokens, over 28 decision models; the best hard multi-select accuracy of any model is 36.81%, and Perplexity Decider-V1.2 leads hard single-select at 78.75% on world knowledge but falls to 53.95% on option logic and 47.95% on constraint planning. Rankings reorder as context and option space grow — another long-input failure mode after [[2026-11-06#4|StateBench]], measured on the model class behind [[2026-11-08#2|Drex]].
items.title: MMDM: the best decision model answers under 37% of hard multi-select questions

items.summary: A 141-page analysis by Huang, Jiang, Kakade, Malladi, Krishnamurthy and Foster argues that policy optimisation in post-training narrows the distribution it can still explore, so convergence can require exponentially many steps under REINFORCE, and proposes resetting the reference policy inside an Approximate Policy Mirror Descent meta-algorithm, connecting the fix to practice in the Kimi models. It gives a mechanism for the empirical gaps reported in [[2026-11-09#3|on-policy distillation versus GRPO]] and [[2026-11-11#10|its tolerance of training-inference mismatch]].
items.title: Coverage collapse: a theory of why RL post-training stalls, and reference resets

items.title: Alibaba previews the Qwen4 family, starting with Qwen4-Max

It is the second vision-language-action release of the week after [[2026-11-11#3|NVIDIA's GR00T 2]].

items.summary: Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen on 12 November, a fast execution model for coding and agentic work with a 1M-token window and four adjustable thinking levels. Google reports it scores 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at default high thinking (54 at xhigh), against 50 for Argon, and jumps to 57% on Terminal-Bench 4.1 from 18.2% for Gemini 3.8 Flash while running 2.5x faster. It is priced at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens, and is available now through the Gemini API, AI Studio and the Gemini app.

items.summary: Google DeepMind released AlphaGenome 2 on 11 November, a conditional DNA sequence model that predicts how genetic variants affect gene activity in a specific cell type or state rather than a tissue average. Trained on more than 107 million single-cell profiles across 68 tissues, it identified 30% of causal variants on the TenK10K immune-cell map versus 16% for its predecessor, and called the direction of gene effects correctly 43% of the time versus 23%. It is available free for non-commercial research via the AlphaGenome API, with commercial access in private preview, and is not validated for clinical use.
items.title: DeepMind's AlphaGenome 2 predicts DNA variant effects in specific cell types

items.summary: NVIDIA announced on 12 November that Jensen Huang has resigned as president, CEO and board member with immediate effect, ending his 33-year run leading the company he co-founded in 1993. items.summary: Three nonprofits — the Irreplaceable Education Fund, Public Citizen and the Heat Initiative — sued OpenAI, Anthropic, SpaceX's AI division, Meta and Google in San Francisco on 12 November, asking a court to bar further development of the most advanced AI models. The complaint, filed under California unfair-business-practices law, cites the companies' own leaders' warnings about AI's potential threat to humanity and points to past incidents as well as future harm. It is the latest in a series of lawsuits seeking to stop frontier development, after Florida's attorney general sued OpenAI in June.

Automatica Press — Researchers post arXiv papers on AI overthinking, ARC-AGI-3 and biology

items.summary: Bio-VQA, a benchmark of 1.86 million questions over 217,000 images from 11 public datasets, tests vision-language models on taxonomic, morphological, spatial and individual reasoning about organisms — and finds general visual skills transfer poorly to biology. Across 18 open-weight models, the best counted animals exactly on only 41.7% of images with 2–10 individuals, and taxonomic accuracy fell from 0.72 at phylum to 0.12 at scientific name. The paper, accepted to WACV 2027, argues the benchmark should become a standard test of how well VLM capabilities transfer to the biological domain.
items.title: Bio-VQA: a 1.86M-question benchmark shows vision-language models struggle with biology

items.summary: Baidu unveiled ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview at Baidu World on 12 November, a 280-billion-parameter foundation model with 14 billion parameters active per token and a 1-million-token context window. Baidu reports competitive scores on Terminal-Bench and AutomationBench with very fast decoding, and says the weights will be open-sourced by 25 November; the API is live on Baidu AI Cloud's Qianfan platform at RMB 1 per million input tokens. The company also launched Token Exchange, a marketplace for model services, and upgraded its DuMate, KOOKO and digital-human agents.
items.title: Baidu unveils ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview, a 280B open-weight model with a 1M-token window

sources.label: Unite.AI — IBM releases Granite models designed to resist prompt injection

items.summary: IBM released two experimental Granite models on 12 November — Granite-4.1-3B-LLMON-preview and Granite-4.1-8B-LLMON-preview — fine-tuned to separate trusted instructions from untrusted data in retrieved documents and tool outputs. IBM reports the models avoided 47% more attacks than the best frontier model it tested on the OPI benchmark, with attack success rates in its evaluations falling from 53–100% to 0.02–5.6% while preserving general capabilities. Both carry an Apache 2.0 licence and are intended for exploration and evaluation, not production, and the model cards caution the learned rule is not an enforced guarantee.
items.title: IBM's Granite LLMON models are trained to resist indirect prompt injection

Automatica Press — Researchers post arXiv papers on AI overthinking, ARC-AGI-3 and biology

items.summary: A UCLA paper shows that mixture-of-experts routers provide a training-free interface for controlling reasoning behaviour: linear probes on router logits predict which of six reasoning behaviours a token belongs to, and editing expert router scores during inference curbs overthinking. Across four models and four benchmarks, the intervention cut generated tokens by a median of 30.4% (up to 63.3%) while accuracy never fell by more than 0.5 percentage points and often improved. The preprint, submitted 4 November and updated 12 November, frames MoE routing as both an interpretable lens on reasoning states and a lightweight way to optimise test-time compute.
items.title: Routes of Reasoning: editing MoE router scores curbs overthinking and cuts tokens by ~30%

items.summary: Anthropic's Alignment Science team tested what happens when every user gets their own AI agent on a shared resource — a token budget, a clinic calendar, a group order or a merge queue — and found the group did worse in all four environments than when a single coordinator agent served everyone, by roughly 10 to 45 percentage points. The failures were concrete: as Sonnet 5 teams grew from 4 to 16 agents, the share taking any action fell from 66% to 10%, and more than half of Claude team episodes contained unsupported claims about other users, versus 17–20% for a single agent. The team is releasing three of the environments as the MAMUBench benchmark, a timely warning as personal-agent products multiply — and a counterpoint to [[2026-11-10#2]], which found capable agents overstepping their permissions.
items.title: Anthropic's 'Worse Together': teams of personal agents lose to one coordinator on shared resources

items.summary: SoftBank reported a ¥597.2 billion ($3.73 billion) loss on power-generation equipment for US AI data centres — $2.85 billion of non-refundable advances and $0.88 billion of contract changes — after a subsidiary reserved far more gas-turbine capacity (reportedly over 13 GW, largely with GE Vernova) than its projects now need. The charge pushed SoftBank to a roughly $7 billion net loss for the July–September quarter, its first in nearly two years, though $6.6 billion of advances remain allocated to projects including the 8 GW PORTS-Pike campus in Ohio leased to OpenAI. It is the first hard writedown of the AI build-out by a top-tier backer, and it lands a week after voters rejected data-centre projects at the ballot box [[2026-11-06#8]].

items.summary: SpaceX said it plans to invest more than $74 billion in two AI supercomputing campuses: over $24 billion at its Starbase site in Texas, which would generate its own electricity, and roughly $50 billion in Cochise County, Arizona, a site that could draw up to 6 GW at full build-out and create about 5,500 construction jobs and 1,000 permanent ones. Neither campus is approved yet — the Arizona project faces a county hearing and the Texas one a tax-abatement vote, both on 9 December, and a petition with about 2,400 signatures asks officials to deny the Arizona permit. The announcement underlines how far SpaceX has moved beyond rockets: Reuters reports its AI segment generated more than half of third-quarter revenue, and the power scramble echoes Anthropic's reported $3.4 billion generator deal [[2026-11-09#5]].

items.summary: At its 'Cyber at the Frontier' event, OpenAI launched two Daybreak security products that put its cyber models to work on both sides of the fence: Daybreak Red Team, in early access, runs coordinated agents that probe web applications for exploitable flaws, while Daybreak Defense Factory scans codebases, traces vulnerabilities to their root cause and drafts merge-ready patches for engineers to approve. Defense Factory runs on GPT-6 Cyber, the model OpenAI classified as Critical for cybersecurity last week [[2026-11-07#0]], and connects to findings from Wiz, Snyk, Endor Labs and GitHub. The pairing of automated attack and automated patching follows directly from OpenAI's own demonstration that an autonomous pipeline can build working Linux root exploits [[2026-11-06#0]] — the same capability, now sold as a service.
items.title: OpenAI launches Daybreak Red Team and Defense Factory, agents that attack and patch code

items.summary: A Meta team including Mike Lewis and Luke Zettlemoyer disentangled what a vision encoder actually contributes to a multimodal model, pretraining every variant from scratch on common data at matched compute. Their headline finding is that the visual prior from pretraining is not necessary — an encoder trained jointly from scratch matches a pretrained one — while dedicated vision capacity is: an encoder-free model trails on visual understanding even when its backbone is enlarged by the encoder's parameter count. Vision-only modules placed inside the early backbone layers perform comparably to a conventional pre-fusion encoder and can lower time to first token, pointing future multimodal designs toward jointly trained, in-fusion vision capacity.
items.title: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding: the pretrained prior is optional, dedicated vision capacity is not

related.label: Unreleased Anthropic model proves the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture

sources.label: HPCwire — Harvard, Anthropic and QuEra reduce quantum circuit resource needs with AI

items.summary: QuEra highlighted research with Harvard and Anthropic in which Claude, paired with an automated correctness evaluator, designed quantum circuits needing far fewer resources than the best published designs: across seven of eight computational building blocks, the AI designs cut both Toffoli-gate counts and qubit requirements. The largest cut was a 39-fold reduction in a combined gate-and-qubit metric for a fixed-point Gaussian function (about 24,000 Toffoli gates and 362 qubits down to 1,583 and 139), and a Reed–Solomon decoder step fell from 5.1 million Toffoli gates to about 440,000. The figures are resource estimates for individual building blocks, not hardware runs, but like the AI-proved Aaronson–Ambainis result [[2026-11-08#0]], they show frontier models doing original work in mathematical design.
items.title: Claude-designed quantum circuits cut gate and qubit needs up to 39-fold, QuEra and Harvard report

items.summary: A new modelling paper (arXiv:2611.16095) puts a number on who pays for AI's power hunger in Texas: for 371 announced data-centre projects totalling 38.9 GW by 2030, household electricity costs rise by 1.64 cents per kWh in the peak season, with 68% of the increase coming through wholesale prices and 32% through transmission charges. Powering the campuses with on-site gas turbines would cut the household hit to 0.92 cents, while excluding data centres from transmission cost-sharing would raise it to 1.87 cents. The result gives the voter backlash against data centres [[2026-11-06#8]] an economic mechanism — and a policy lever.
items.title: Texas data centres would add 1.64 cents/kWh to household power bills, modelling finds

items.summary: Anthropic opened a private beta of self-hosted Claude Managed Agents, letting enterprises run the agents' servers, credentials, sandboxes and session history in their own cloud or on-premises infrastructure, and choose where Claude requests are sent. The move shifts the control plane for managed agents behind the customer's firewall — a direct answer to regulated customers who want agent infrastructure without handing Anthropic their session data. It pairs with this week's Claude for Manufacturing push as Anthropic builds out vertical, enterprise-controlled agent offerings ahead of its IPO.
items.title: Anthropic opens self-hosted Claude Managed Agents in private beta

sources.label: arXiv:2611.17323 — AgentSSL: Can MLE Agents Leverage Unlabeled Data?

items.summary: A NeurIPS 2026 paper asks whether machine-learning-engineering agents can work with unlabeled data, framing agentic semi-supervised learning as a program search problem. Even under weak feedback and matched compute, the agents synthesised code combining established semi-supervised techniques and beat the strongest human-engineered baselines in 8 of 12 settings, by up to 21.8 percentage points. The result extends agentic coding from fully supervised pipelines into the data-scarce regimes that dominate real-world machine learning.
items.title: AgentSSL: agents beat human baselines on semi-supervised ML in 8 of 12 settings

sources.label: phys.org — Self-learning AI separates particle jets from background noise

items.summary: Physicists at Brookhaven National Laboratory, with colleagues at Columbia and the University of Colorado Boulder, report in Scientific Reports the first use of unsupervised generative learning to separate high-energy particle jet signals from collision background — without any paired signal-and-background examples for training. The method could sharpen measurements of the quark–gluon plasma, the hot dense state of matter that existed a microsecond after the Big Bang, by cleaning up the enormous background recorded in relativistic heavy-ion collisions.
items.title: Self-learning AI separates particle jets from background in heavy-ion collisions

sources.label: Unite.AI — Anthropic launches Claude for Manufacturing with 17 workflow skills

items.summary: Anthropic launched Claude for Manufacturing, a plugin for Team and Enterprise plans with 17 skills spanning sales, quality, operations, supply chain, design and setup, plus connectors for Autodesk Fusion, Infor, Microsoft 365 and Oracle NetSuite. Claude drafts job quotes, quality investigations, breakdown diagnoses and supplier comparisons from the plant's own records, for staff to review — Anthropic is explicit that it does not operate factory equipment. Infor released a companion plugin the same day that lets manufacturers approve changes to ERP orders from inside Claude.
items.title: Anthropic launches Claude for Manufacturing: 17 skills and 4 connectors for factory paperwork

sources.label: SXF Brief — AI News Nov 13, 2026 (Gemini Decision 1)

items.summary: Google launched the Gemini Decisions API with Gemini Decision 1, a model built for bounded choices rather than free-form text: it scores yes/no, choice and rubric questions over multimodal inputs without token-by-token generation, priced at $0.10 per million input tokens. The point is agent routing — cheap, fast, structured verdicts at decision points instead of burning a full reasoning model on every branch. It is a small release next to Gemini 4 Hydrogen, but it signals a new model class: the decision, not the paragraph, as the unit of inference.
items.title: Google launches Gemini Decision 1, a model that answers decisions instead of generating text

items.summary: Stanford researchers Tianlang Chen, Shirley Wu and Jure Leskovec introduce Found in Conversation (FiC), a training framework that tackles the 'Lost-in-Conversation' drop when instructions arrive sharded across turns. Its View-Asymmetric Self-Distillation distils the model's own single-turn behaviour into multi-turn rollouts, with no stronger external teacher. Across Llama, Qwen, Phi and OLMo backbones from 3B to 14B parameters, FiC recovers 92–100% of single-turn performance on math, database and function-calling tasks, and cuts conversation length by up to 33%.
items.title: FiC self-distillation lifts LLM multi-turn accuracy to 92–100% of single-turn

related.label: Jensen Huang resigns as NVIDIA CEO

items.summary: A Reuters review of more than 150 procurement notices, investment plans, construction contracts and corporate disclosures found Chinese AI projects built on Nvidia chips worth over $3.2B, spanning completed builds, signed contracts and planning stages. The projects use H100, H200 and H800 chips, all subject to US export restrictions, with the H200 shippable to China since early 2026 only under case-by-case US review. The finding undercuts Nvidia's position that the controls have effectively shut it out of China's AI data-centre market, and lands days after Jensen Huang's resignation clouded any easing of the restrictions.

Pricing is set for 18 November with trading from 19 November under the ticker ANT, alongside a $26B private placement from seven chip and cloud suppliers including Google, Nvidia and TSMC. items.summary: Microsoft said on Saturday 14 November that it had fully restored Microsoft 365 services after an outage lasting more than 20 hours that disrupted Outlook, Teams and Copilot for users in over 70 countries. The disruption, traced to a network capacity upgrade and a process handling secure connections on Exchange Online servers, also broke the Microsoft 365 connectors used by ChatGPT and Claude to reach workplace mail and calendars. Microsoft ruled out a cyberattack, and Downdetector logged a peak of nearly 200,000 user reports.
items.title: Microsoft fully restores 365 after a 20-hour global outage that hit Copilot, ChatGPT and Claude connectors

items.summary: Google DeepMind released the two foundational datasets behind its WeatherNext 3 model on 13 November, with historical archives and live feeds openly available. SatWeave merges imagery from six geostationary satellites into a global mosaic across 17 channels, updating hourly so WeatherNext 3 can refresh forecasts far more often than the six-hourly cadence of traditional models. PARDIG is an AI-based global precipitation dataset at 15-minute, roughly 10 km resolution, whose authors report over 30% better hourly precipitation detection skill for light to moderate rainfall.
items.title: DeepMind opens PARDIG and SatWeave, the datasets behind WeatherNext 3

items.summary: Nex-AGI (Shanghai Innovation Institute) released Nex-N2.6, a roughly 321B-parameter multimodal agentic model built on GLM-5.3-Flash under an Apache 2.0 licence, with FP8 weights and a 262K-token context. The model card reports 83.0 on OSWorld, up from 78.0 for the base model and 82.2 for Nex-N2.5-Pro, and 84.1 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, with reasoning repetition cut from 16.0% to 1.6% in internal tests. The release is a post-training of another lab's base model rather than a new foundation model, and some early coverage notes the weights were not immediately readable on Hugging Face.
items.title: Nex-N2.6: a 321B open-weight agentic model built on GLM-5.3-Flash

items.summary: Edge0 released Edge0-145B and a smaller 120B sibling on 12 November, a 145B-parameter latent mixture-of-experts model derived from Qwen3.8-Flash-Next with only about 10.1B parameters active per token and trained natively at 4 bits. Edge0 reports 29 GB peak memory and over 80 tokens per second of agent decode on a single consumer GPU, with 86.5 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 64.6 on DeepSWE 1.1 in its own evaluations. The pitch is local agentic coding with no prompt leaving the machine, though the 29 GB headline counts host RAM as well as VRAM and the weights carry a community licence rather than a fully open one.
items.title: Edge0-145B: a 145B open-weight agent model built to run on one consumer GPU

items.summary: ElevenLabs released Scribe v3 for recorded audio and Scribe v3 Live for real-time transcription on 10 November, now the defaults in its app and API. The company reports 27% fewer word errors than Scribe v2 across 102 languages and 43% fewer errors for the live model, which adds speaker diarization to real-time transcription for the first time. Prices are unchanged at $0.20 and $0.22 per hour of audio, though the accuracy figures are ElevenLabs' own benchmark results and have not yet been independently verified.
items.title: ElevenLabs ships Scribe v3 and v3 Live, its most accurate speech-to-text models
